candidate.hypothesis: Allow retained drafts to be corrected after definitive rejection

The configured Playwright matcher ignores the enabled option of toBeEnabled. The assertion consequently expects the Edit preferences button to be enabled even for the read-only and uncertain stories, so the catalog test fails.

result.reason: The assertion supplies false for precisely the stories whose preferences control is false. Whether this causes failure depends on the locked matcher's handling of enabled:false, not its name. Version-matched official matcher source was unavailable, so neither ignoring the option nor the alleged resulting test failure is established.
result.missing: Official implementation evidence for playwright 1.64.1, used by the locked @playwright/test package, showing how toBeEnabled handles options.enabled=false. The playwright release was resolved from the lockfile but its official source was unavailable; @playwright/test lookups returned official-version-not-proven.

premises.claim: The catalog script runs catalog.spec.ts, which imports expect directly from @playwright/test.
The frontend locks @playwright/test and playwright to 1.64.1; the locked test package depends on playwright 1.64.1.
The administration test includes read-only and uncertain and explicitly passes enabled:false for both to the Edit preferences assertion.
The ReadOnly and Uncertain story exports select those examples, whose fixture sets controls.preferences to false.
The component passes controls.preferences to its editPreferences button helper, whose template binds disabled to the inverse of that value.

result.reason: The repository supports the suspected one-way sent-latch defect: if the submitted draft survives rejection, Back and editing remain blocked even though rejected records are not unresolved-request blockers. Reset replaces the draft rather than correcting its retained values. However, proving the observable page route requires establishing component retention across Lit-driven view updates. Version-matched official evidence for that material behavior could not be established, so the end-to-end hypothesis remains inconclusive.
result.missing: Official lookups for the locked lit-html 3.3.3 and lit-element 4.2.2 returned official-version-not-proven, including with exact lockfile resolution entries. Matching renderer/lifecycle evidence is needed to establish that the same administration instance and draft survive the actual submission/rejection view transitions.

premises.claim: Saving a reviewed draft sets sent=true before dispatching its submission intent.
For a retained sent draft, change/check/review handlers refuse input, and the review template disables Back and Save independently of the outcome.
The component update hook clears drafts for retirement, invalid non-null scope or changed owner; it has no rejected-outcome unlock.
The controller's unresolved-request edit guard checks prepared and uncertain records, not rejected records.
The controller maps rejected outcomes to the journal's rejected stage.
Reset calls open, whose member-update payload comes from current roster data and whose new unsent draft replaces the map entry; it does not restore editing of the retained payload.
The parent template contains an unconditional administration element receiving view, pending and retired property bindings.
The frontend pins Lit 3.3.3; its lockfile selects lit-element 4.2.2 and lit-html 3.3.3.
